title: Canonical composition and identity comparisons on enlarged etale sites
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use the enlarged etale sites $\mathcal C_X$ of chartwise etale algebraic spaces over $X$ and the continuous base-change functors $v_f:\mathcal C_Y\to\mathcal C_X$, $V\mapsto X\times_YV$, of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. For morphisms $W\xrightarrow{g}X\xrightarrow{f}Y$, define the composition comparison $v_g\circ v_f\simeq v_{f\circ g}$ on $V\to Y$ to be the fibre-product isomorphism $W\times_X(X\times_YV)\simeq W\times_YV$ preserving the projections, and define the identity comparison $v_{\mathrm{id}_X}\simeq\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C_X}$ on $V\to X$ to be the second projection $X\times_XV\to V$. The products are the existing sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For any coefficient category $A$ and its sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], write $f_*G(V)=G(X\times_YV)$ for direct image. Define the direct-image comparisons $f_*g_*\simeq(f\circ g)_*$ and $(\mathrm{id}_X)_*\simeq\mathrm{id}$ by applying each sheaf contravariantly to these projection-preserving site comparisons. Finally, for any specified family of left adjoints $L_f\dashv f_*$, use the composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] and conjugation of adjoint isomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] to define $L_g\circ L_f\simeq L_{f\circ g}$ as the adjunction-compatible conjugate of the inverse direct-image composition comparison. These are definitions of the comparison maps; their coherence assertions and the compatibility of structural ring maps are not additional data or hypotheses.

def enlargedInverseCompositionIso (A : Type v) [Category.{w} A]
    (L : ∀ (X Y : AlgebraicSpace S), (X ⟶ Y) →
      Sheaf Y.enlargedEtaleTopology A ⥤ Sheaf X.enlargedEtaleTopology A)
    (adj : ∀ {X Y : AlgebraicSpace S} (f : X ⟶ Y), L X Y f ⊣ enlargedDirectImage f A)
    {W X Y : AlgebraicSpace S} (g : W ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    L X Y f ⋙ L W X g ≅ L W Y (g ≫ f)
